answer: No. The pre‑2024 version of Regulation 16(1)(c) permits borrowing only to meet temporary funding requirements (up to 30 days, no more than four occasions a year and not more than 10 % of investable funds). The post‑2024 version adds borrowing for day‑to‑day operational requirements in addition to temporary funding, while keeping the same limits. Therefore the scope of permissible borrowing is broader after 2024.

answer: An indirect acquisition is treated as a direct acquisition for all purposes when any one of the following exceeds eighty per cent: (a) the proportionate net asset value of the target company as a percentage of the consolidated NAV, (b) the proportionate sales turnover as a percentage of consolidated sales turnover, or (c) the proportionate market capitalisation as a percentage of enterprise value of the entity being acquired.

citations.quote: Regulation 5(2): In case of an indirect acquisition where (a) the proportionate net asset value of the target company as a percentage of the consolidated NAV, (b) the proportionate sales turnover as a percentage of consolidated sales turnover, or (c) the proportionate market capitalisation as a percentage of enterprise value of the entity being acquired is in excess of eighty per cent, such indirect acquisition shall be regarded as a direct acquisition for all purposes including timing, pricing and compliance requirements.
